subject: On-prem K8s: disk topology, eviction & node inventory review
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@edgeco.com>
To: mateo_alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya R. <infra@edgeco.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: K8s disk topology + eviction planning for on-prem pilot

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the call earlier. As we discussed, we're getting the on-prem pilot ready and want Redwood to validate our cluster inventory and the disk/eviction strategy before we hand over to SRE. Attached is a CSV with current host specs (CPUs, RAM, local disks) and a draft network diagram. Key asks: 

- Can you confirm recommended PV layout (local SSD vs network PV) for model-serving GPU nodes?
- Best-practice kubelet eviction thresholds for mixed-use nodes (inference + system pods).
- Guidance on using taints/tolerations for GPU vs non-GPU pools.

We're aiming for a non-production pilot (300 concurrent inference qps) in the first week of May. Pls loop in anyone on your side who should see this.

Thanks,
Samir Shah
Infrastructure Lead, EdgeCo
Attachments: edgeco_hw_inventory.csv, proposed-network-diagram.png

From: mateo_alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@edgeco.com>
Cc: Maya R. <infra@edgeco.com>, dev_patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: K8s disk topology + eviction planning for on-prem pilot

Samir —

Thanks for the inventory. Quick read of the CSV looks good; sending an initial checklist below and will follow with a short matrix of tradeoffs. Dev, looping you for kernel / kubelet tuning and node pool recommendations.

Quick checklist (high level):
- GPU nodes: keep model artifacts and LM KV cache on local NVMe (fast local disks). Use an NFS-backed PV class for long-term model storage only.
- Non-GPU nodes (API, control-plane-proxied): use network PVs (Ceph/Rook) with 3x replication for durability.
- Kubelet eviction: set ephemeral-storage eviction at 10% free or 5Gi (whichever higher) for inference-critical nodes; reduce system-reserved for GPU nodes to avoid OOM eviction.
- Node pools: dedicated gpu-large (taint: dedicated=ai:NoSchedule), gpu-small (for batch jobs), general-purpose (no taint).
- PVC reclaim policy: Retain for GPU local model volumes if you want to preserve caches across node replacement.

I'll prepare a short matrix by EOD. In parallel, can you confirm whether you prefer hostPath + local-volume-provisioner or a local CSI driver (recommended) for the NVMe on GPU hosts?

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Solution Architect, Redwood Inference

From: dev_patel <dev@redwood.ai>
To: mateo_alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>, Samir Shah <samir.shah@edgeco.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: K8s disk topology + eviction planning for on-prem pilot

Samir, Mateo —

Adding concrete node sizing + kubelet knobs from our bench tests: 

Node pools (recommended):
- gpu-1 (p4-like equiv): 8 GPUs, 512Gi RAM, local NVMe (1-2TB) mounted via CSI-localpv; taint: redwood.ai/gpu=true
- gpu-2 (inference-small): 1-2 GPUs, 192-256Gi RAM, local NVMe (512GB); for lower-concurrency microservices
- mgmt-general: 16 CPUs, 64Gi RAM, network PVs for logging/metrics

Kubelet config snippets (examples):
- evictionHard: 
  memory.available: "200Mi"
  nodefs.available: "1Gi"
  nodefs.inodesFree: "5%"
  imagefs.available: "2Gi"
- evictionSoft (with grace):
  memory.available: "500Mi"
  nodefs.available: "5%"
  gracePeriod: "2m"

Notes:
- Use ephemeral-storage QoS: reserve 10% on gpu nodes to avoid model cache thrash during heavy loads.
- Local CSI driver gives better lifecycle and PV semantics than hostPath; we recommend local-volume provisioner + CSI for production-like behavior.

I'll attach a sample kubelet-config.yaml and a unit test we run in staging.

—Dev Patel
Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: kubelet-config-example.yaml (stub)

From: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@edgeco.com>, mateo_alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: K8s disk topology + eviction planning for on-prem pilot

Folks — quick compliance note before we finalize PV lifecycles: 

- Encryption: ensure local NVMe full-disk encryption (either at OS-level LUKS or vendor HSM integration) for any node storing model artifacts containing customer PII.
- KMS: we recommend integrating with your KMS for envelope keys; Redwood supports both AWS KMS and HashiCorp Vault—please confirm what you run in your DC.
- Audit logs: persist kube-apiserver audit logs to a network PV (retention 365 days) and stream copies to your SIEM.

Samir — can you share whether EdgeCo requires FIPS modes or HSM-backed keys? That will affect our recommended CSI driver and node image.

—Lauren Bishop
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@edgeco.com>
To: mateo_alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya R. <infra@edgeco.com>, dev_patel <dev@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: K8s disk topology + eviction planning for on-prem pilot

Thanks team — this is exactly what we needed. A couple of quick answers: 

- We'll use a local CSI driver (vendor image supported by our hardware OEM).
- EdgeCo runs Vault for KMS (no HSM for pilot; FIPS not required initially).
- We'll enable host-level LUKS on NVMe with keys managed by Vault.

Next steps:
1) We'll flip the hw_inventory to the shared Drive folder and tag who owns each host.
2) Schedule an infra dry-run week of 25 Apr (internal), and we'll invite Redwood for a join on 26 Apr.
3) Samir to open the JIRA (EDGE-1204) with the final host list by 16 Apr.

Appreciate the quick turnaround. We'll share the updated CSV and network diagram shortly.

—Samir
Samir Shah
Infrastructure Lead, EdgeCo
Attachments: pv-retention-and-reclaim-policy.docx
